_comment: Copy to baseline.config.json at your repo root. The runner auto-detects sensible defaults; override only what you need. Every rule in the set is a deterministic read of repo files, AND-gated to one exit code — there is no warn tier and no opt-in pack. Two opt-ins remain, with opposite defaults: the trust circle (the plugins below — opt IN, default out) and the baseline rules layer (every other rule — opt OUT, default in).
_project_type: node | service | python | library | docs. Only narrows which rules apply to this repo; it activates nothing.
_baseline_rules: THE BASELINE RULES LAYER — the second opt-in, and the only one that is IN by default. Every rule that is not a plugin rule (BUILD, GOV, SEC — the tree reads any repo can answer) is one layer you opt in or out of at setup time. Absent key = IN, because the baseline is what you get by standing still; `true` says the same thing out loud. `false` opts the layer OUT: those rules resolve n/a, produce no finding and are excluded from the exit gate — the same treatment an unadopted plugin gets. It can never hide a failure silently: `baseline check` prints the layer state (and, when OUT, every muted rule id) on every run, and `--json` carries it as `baseline`. `baseline trust setup --baseline-rules in|out` writes it (opting IN deletes the key, since absent IS in).
_plugins: PLUG-01..03 — the trust circle: the opt-IN half of the rule set (the baseline rules layer above is the opt-OUT half). MEMBERSHIP IS THE KEY: naming a plugin here adopts it, and its rule becomes a blocker in your CI — the artifact must be present and git must say what `ignored` expects. A plugin you do NOT name is a SUGGESTION: baseline offers it in the report, its rule resolves n/a, and it can never fail your build. So delete a line to drop a tool; `{}` adopts at the defaults; `false` records a decision not to. `baseline trust add <tool>` / `baseline trust remove <tool>` edit exactly this object, and `baseline trust setup` prints the recommended circle. okf-rag's path comes from $BASELINE_OKF_BUNDLE unless set here (the env var sets a member's path, it never creates membership — CI clones tracked files, not a shell), and the gitignore question is skipped when the path is outside the repo. baseline reads the artifact's metadata only (exists, file-or-dir, mtime, gitignore state), never its content; a finding writes .baseline/log/PLUG-0N.log.
_sources_of_truth: one declared home per fact class (status, decisions, ...), so a reader knows where each kind of truth lives. Documentary: no rule reads it since the v4 cut.
_retired_keys: bootstrap_command, command_timeout_ms, claims_file, decision_globs, doc_globs, doc_lag_days, doc_freshness_days, freshness_globs, generated_globs, grounding_docs and prior_art_recheck_days went with the rules that read them. A config still naming one is inert, never an error.
